translations.text: Our Father, who art in heaven. Our Father, who is in heaven.
It is a great grace that a man may call the almighty Lord his father. Hallowed be thy name. May your name be hallowed.
We have no need to pray that his name be hallowed, except that we pray often that it be hallowed in us: that we keep the holiness
that we received from him in baptism, so that we may bring it, kept safe, before him on the day of judgment. Thy kingdom come. May your kingdom come.
His kingdom alone has always been; but we must pray to the almighty Lord that he rule in us, and not the devil's temptation. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
May your will be done, as it is in heaven, so also on earth: that as blamelessly and as worthily as your angels fulfil your will in heaven, we may fulfil it in the same measure on earth.
Give us this day our daily bread. Give us our daily bread.
For this we must pray to the almighty Lord: that his body and his blood, which we receive from the altar, may come to us for eternal salvation rather than for punishment.
And forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
Everyone must take these words to heart: that every man should forgive his brother and his fellow their debts, so that the almighty Lord will then forgive us ours.
Whoever forgives his fellow his debts may then pray that the Lord forgive him his own, when he says: "Forgive me, as I forgive others."
And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. And do not lead us into temptation, but free us from all sins.
For this we must pray to the Lord: that he not let the devil tempt us as far as the devil's evil will desires, but only as far as we can overcome with your grace.
